doc.title: Dick Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: What inspires Hamilton alumni loyalty and Milt Fillius
summary: Sherman credits the campus, faculty and Winton Tolles; Monk talks about his daughter at Hamilton and Milt Fillius's role in the archive.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Right, well just to wrap up, I’ve been always impressed by the loyalty and passion of Hamilton alums, the ones that don’t have it I haven’t met, so, you know, but the ones that I have, starting with Milt Fillius and I go what is it about this place that inspires that kind of loyalty.

It’s not one thing it’s a combination of things. There’s a beauty of the physical plant — you have the campus and Root Glen and things second to none. You have I think a marvelous faculty, in my day you did, and I think that we had a good administration, we had Winton Tolles. So the people who went to college in my day at Hamilton loved the college. They were enthusiastic then and as alums they become very enthusiastic. You’ll see them howling with delight when they hear our band playing.
Well that’s great. And some of that hasn’t changed because when I hear my daughter talk to other people about the college she will say that. She’ll say, “Oh, I loved Hamilton.”
I’m interested in what is her response. What were the elements that she praised?

You know I’m not sure yet because she won’t say it to my wife and I as much as she will to another person. But she loved the camaraderie. I think she benefited from rubbing elbows with people from other socioeconomic strata — whatever you want to call that.
Yeah.
And she was an RA for three years so she learned a great deal about responsibility.
Interesting. Maybe she’ll come forth with some more opinions after she has aged a little bit.
I’m sure she will.
You seem to be a happy man here at Hamilton.

Well you know one thing, this has been a dream gig for me, and Milt Fillius used to joke, he wasn’t joking, he used to put in a joke, he said, “I wanted the job that I gave to you.” He made this whole interview thing possible, and since then I’ve met so many of my musical heroes, and it’s been a great job for me.
What a good way to look at it.
And he wanted to do it.
I’m glad you got it.
Yeah, okay.
I don’t know how good he would have been. He probably would have been fine but —

He did sit in on a few early on. We interviewed Mona Hinton, Milt Hinton’s wife, together, and a couple others. And he probably — he was a very opinionated man, about his musical tastes, so if he didn’t like something he was not good at disguising it.
I gathered that, yes.
But he has a good legacy. So I want to thank you for your conversation today.
Oh I enjoyed it, Monk.
